Subject: Post-call recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs / next steps

Hi Sophie — great discussion earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the perf run:

Key requirements you confirmed on the call:
- TTFT target (time-to-first-token): <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) — goal is 200–250ms for the most latency-sensitive flows.
- Streaming behavior: must return partial content as soon as available; preferred implementation: SSE or WebSocket (both OK; you said SSE is simpler for your infra).
- Chunk cadence: ideally first chunk within TTFT target, subsequent chunks every ~200–300ms for natural language responses.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 150 RPS ingestion with 20 concurrent user sessions; peak bursts up to 300 RPS for short periods.
- SLOs: availability + latency targets important for your compliance team (we'll propose SLA language).

Action items I propose:
1) Redwood to run a focused perf validation (POC) against a representative prompt set and model variant. We'll measure TTFT, chunk cadence, throughput, and error rate.
2) Marissa to share a perf test plan and recommended protocol (SSE vs WebSocket) and suggested config (batching, KV cache, warmup).
3) Acme to provide 10 representative prompts and a spike profile (expected RPS distribution) so we can reproduce traffic characteristics.
4) I'll send an updated mutual action plan and an SLA draft for review — if those look good we can schedule the perf run next week.

Attachments: 20260224-mutual_action_plan.pdf (draft)

Thanks, and LMK which days next week work for the perf run (we recommend Tue/Wed morning PT).

Best,

Thanks Aditya — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over prompts:

- For TTFT: our internal requirement is <= 300ms 95th percentile for the real-time chat path. If you can target 250ms p95 in the POC, that's ideal.
- For streaming: SSE is preferred for now because our frontend uses an EventSource-based client. WebSocket is an option if you recommend it for better bi-directional flow control.
- Regarding chunk cadence: 200–300ms cadence is a good target; we care more about responsiveness than maximizing chunk size.
- Error behavior: we need to understand how Redwood handles partial failures (e.g., model fallback, retries) and how that affects TTFT & user experience.

I'll get the 10 representative prompts to you by end of day Friday and share the spike profile. Let's tentatively slot Wednesday next week (3/4) 9:30am PT for the perf run.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TTFT & streaming SLOs / next steps — perf test plan

Hi Sophie — thanks for the details and the preferred times. Quick technical notes and what we'll measure in the POC: 

1) Protocol:
- SSE (EventSource) is perfectly viable for your use case and simpler to integrate. It is uni-directional (server->client) which is fine if you do not need mid-stream client messages.
- WebSocket gives lower overhead for long-lived sessions and makes bi-directional control messages easier (e.g., incremental stops/edits). If frontend can add a small client lib, WS is my recommendation when p95 TTFT tighter than ~200ms or when you expect many mid-stream client control messages.

2) TTFT definition & measurement:
- We'll measure TTFT as time from request arrival at Redwood ingress to the first token emitted to the client (inclusive of any network hop inside Redwood).
- For the POC we'll collect p50/p90/p95 for TTFT and for first-chunk size. We'll also measure chunk cadence (time between emitted token batches).

3) Expected numbers & config levers:
- In our tests, small prompt + gpt-style 7B variants return TTFT in ~120–250ms when run on optimized nodes with KV cache warmed and minimal batching.
- Batching increases throughput but increases TTFT; we'll tune batching to meet your TTFT SLO while achieving 150 RPS baseline.
- Suggested POC config: target concurrency 20, sustained RPS 150, short spikes to 300 RPS for 2–3 minutes. Warm-up phase of 5 minutes recommended to prime caches.

4) Failure & fallback behavior:
- Redwood can be configured to cascade to a lower-cost/lower-latency model variant on failures. We'll report how fallbacks affect TTFT and provide a recommended policy (canary threshold).

5) Data & compliance:
- We'll use your requested retention & audit settings during the POC. Please confirm if any PII must be scrubbed before we ingest prompts.

I've attached the perf test plan with the exact scenarios and measurement scripts: 20260302-perf_test_plan.md.

Proposed next step: run the perf test Wednesday 3/4 at 9:30am PT. We'll stream results into the shared doc and do a short sync after the run to review metrics.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
